motivering: C champions freedom of choice and efficiency in health and social care, and effective pharmacy supervision is central to patient safety. C's own motions 1 and 2 (Anders W Jonsson et al.) on improved oversight of pharmacy supervision were rejected by the committee. C should support Reservation 1 and vote No against the committee's proposal to note the written communication.

citations.quote: We want to defend freedom of choice in health and social care and conduct activities close to those receiving care. Responsibility for healthcare must not be transferred from the regions to the state.
citations.princip: freedom of choice and efficiency in healthcare

citations.quote: We want to open up for more healthcare providers and increase freedom of choice so that patients, together with their doctor, can choose their healthcare provider and the time when an operation or treatment best suits the patient's needs.
citations.princip: freedom of choice and competition in the healthcare sector

motivering: The Centre Party wants to create freer markets and improve competition. An independent dispute resolution system for collective rent negotiations creates a more efficient and predictable rental market, in line with C's market orientation and decentralisation ambitions. V's motions on alternative solutions lack support in C's documents and are rejected.

citations.quote: By creating freer markets and improving competition, we can dampen prices further.
Decentralise more. People should be able to decide more for themselves, and political decisions should be made close to those affected.

motivering: C has its own motions (Ulrika Heie et al. motions 1, 4 and 5 and Annie Lööf et al. motion 71) that the committee wishes to reject. In addition, the committee issues a tillkännagivande (formal request) against building high-speed rail, which directly contradicts the manifesto's promise to build new main lines. C votes No to uphold its railway policy and its own motions.

citations.quote: We want to upgrade regional railways, build new main lines from north to south, raise the standard of the national main rail network across the entire country, and make a major investment in tomorrow's rail traffic — for the good of the climate and the countryside.
citations.princip: main rail lines and rail investment

citations.quote: The whole country is needed, from suburb to industrial town, from city to countryside. All parts of Sweden shall see increased freedom, security, and accessibility during the next term of government.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motions (Niels Paarup-Petersen et al. (C) motions 2 and 12–15) in the cyber policy matter that the committee proposes to reject. The manifesto demands that Sweden strengthens its total defence (totalförsvar), which includes cyber capability. Reservation 12 constitutes C's own position and the party should vote No to support it.

citations.quote: We need to strengthen Sweden's total defence, reinforce the entire chain of justice, invest in preventive measures, and ensure an equitable school system.

Sweden shall be defended. We want to strengthen the military defence quickly, forcefully, and for the long term. Sweden needs to spend two percent of GDP on defence as soon as practically possible and join NATO.

motivering: C has submitted motion 4 on objectives and performance reporting for the defence budget, likely including demands for faster achievement of the 2% target. Reservation 1 (Alternative A) is interpreted as C's reservation. The committee's proposal rejects C's motion 4, and the party therefore supports its reservation and votes No.

citations.quote: Sweden shall be defended. We want to strengthen the military defence quickly, forcefully, and for the long term. Sweden needs to spend two percent of GDP on defence as soon as practically possible and join NATO.
Civil defence is also vital. We must strengthen civil defence and society's preparedness for war and crisis.

motivering: The committee rejects SD's motion on the prohibition on distraint (utmätningsförbudet). C has no motion in the vote and the manifesto lacks a specific position on distraint. Without a clear reason to support SD's reservation, and without C's rule-of-law principles supporting the specific content of the motion, C votes with the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: The rule of law and the individual's rights vis-à-vis the state must be defended.

motivering: The proposal introduces a sustainability objective for the Seventh AP Fund (Sjunde AP-fonden) and strengthens the governance of the default option, which is well in line with the party's commitments on the sustainability of the pension system and ambitious climate and environmental work. Rejecting the Left Party's reservation is natural for the Centre Party, which has consistently distanced itself from V's economic policy and instead supports market-oriented pension solutions.

citations.quote: We must defend the long-term fairness and sustainability of the pension system.
The Centre Party puts the climate first, because the future must be green.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motions (Annie Lööf motions 25–26, Jonny Cato motions 10–11) on the establishment of newly arrived women that the committee wishes to reject. The manifesto is explicit: more foreign-born women must be given the chance to work and be intensively integrated. No means that the party supports its reservation and its own motions on faster and more intensive integration.

citations.quote: More foreign-born women must have the chance to work, learn Swedish, and fully enter Swedish society. This is a gain for both the individual and society at large.
Create an intensive year for faster integration. Those who receive a residence permit shall be quickly integrated and given the opportunity to support themselves.

motivering: C has actively pushed through a 'historic labour market reform' for increased flexibility and does not want to see new restrictions on fixed-term employment or the hiring out of workers. The committee rejects V's and MP's motions, which likely aim at increased restrictions. The committee's proposal is consistent with C's liberal line for a flexible labour market.

citations.quote: During the last term of government, the Centre Party pushed through a historic labour market reform that entails greater flexibility for companies and better transition opportunities for employees. We will continue the work towards a labour market that works even better for both employers and employees.
The Swedish labour market needs both more flexibility and more security. Support for transition and further training must improve.

motivering: The Centre Party believes that liberal democracy should be protected from both internal and external threats, including terrorism. The constitutional amendment enables ordinary law against associations that support terrorist activities, which falls within the party's security and democracy-protection agenda. Since the only parliamentary decision on this dormant proposal was taken in April 2022, the party should be consistent and confirm it at the mandatory second occasion.

citations.quote: liberal democracy is under threat. We must never take it for granted or underestimate its adversaries.
Society must not yield to the gangs.

motivering: The committee rejects the Centre Party's own motions (Kerstin Lundgren motion 55 and Annie Lööf motion 144) on women's participation in post-conflict reconstruction. C supports Reservation 2. The party's strong focus on gender equality and women's empowerment as a core liberal principle underpins this position.

citations.quote: We can create a more gender-equal Sweden that strengthens women's empowerment
We are liberals because we believe in the freedom of the individual and the equal worth of all. A society without gender equality is not fully free
citations.princip: gender equality as a core liberal value

motivering: The Centre Party's integration policy emphasises requirements, work, and rapid establishment in the labour market rather than expanding the target group of state programmes. V's, MP's, and S's motions on the target group of the establishment programme (etableringsprogrammet) reflect a more expansive state-oriented approach that differs from C's work-first (arbetslinjen) approach. C supports the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Integration efforts must be characterised by hard work and high expectations. Newly arrived immigrants should qualify their way into the social security systems.
Those who receive a residence permit shall be quickly integrated and given the opportunity to support themselves.

motivering: The committee proposes to reject a specific SD motion on gambling regulation. The Centre Party has explicitly committed not to cooperate with the Sweden Democrats or give them influence over policy. The party also has no specific gambling regulation positions in its manifesto that support the SD alternative, and supports the committee's majority position.

citations.quote: The Centre Party is now the only centre-right party that will not cooperate with the Sweden Democrats or give them power over how Sweden is governed.

motivering: C has its own motion (Christofer Bergenblock et al., item 25 on paratransit (färdtjänst)) that the committee wishes to reject. The manifesto states that people with disabilities must receive the support they need and that welfare must be equal throughout the country. C votes No to support its motion on accessible paratransit.

citations.quote: If you have a disability, you shall receive the support you need, and the state shall take greater responsibility for ensuring that the LSS (Act on Support and Service for Persons with Certain Functional Impairments) works.
All residents shall have access to equal and reliable welfare regardless of where they live, and public services shall be there when needed.

motivering: Criminalising foreign espionage strengthens Sweden's security against the direct threat exemplified by Russia's war of aggression. The committee has already removed the most controversial provisions (chapter 27, section 2) that could concern preventive surveillance, which the Centre Party opposes. The remaining proposal supports national security without the restrictions on individual rights the party explicitly rejects.

citations.quote: Sweden must be defended. Russia's invasion, which is in violation of international law, has shown that we cannot rule out Sweden being drawn into war.
We therefore say no to stop-and-search zones, collective punishment, reversed burden of proof, anonymous witnesses, preventive surveillance, and restrictions on freedom of religion.

omvarld.faktor: Russia's ongoing invasion of Ukraine
omvarld.effekt: Elevated security threat level justifies criminalising foreign espionage, despite a general restrictiveness towards expanded state surveillance

motivering: The committee rejects SD's motions (items 6, 9 and 10) on chemicals policy, citing that Sweden already conducts consistent work in this area. The Centre Party has no motions of its own on this matter and is not party to reservation 9. Finding existing work sufficient is consistent with C's environmental policy line.

citations.quote: Sweden shall become the world's most resource-efficient country and the economy more circular.

motivering: The Centre Party upholds freedom of choice in health and social care and wants the regions to retain responsibility for their healthcare contracts. The government's proposal to legislate mandatory contract clauses for private healthcare providers with insurance mandates constitutes state intervention in the regions' contracting. The principle that responsibility must not be transferred from the regions to the state supports approving the committee's decision to reject the government bill in this part.

citations.quote: We want to defend freedom of choice in health and social care and conduct activities close to care recipients. Responsibility for healthcare must not be transferred from the regions to the state.

We want to open up for more healthcare providers and increase freedom of choice so that patients, together with their doctor, can choose provider and the time when an operation or treatment best suits the patient's needs.
citations.princip: more private healthcare providers and freedom of choice

motivering: The Centre Party places high priority on climate but favours market-based instruments such as the EU's emissions trading system over legislated investment prohibitions for the AP funds (the Swedish national pension funds). A specific restriction on the AP funds' mandate to exclude companies that lobby for fossil energy is a more detailed-control intervention than what the party's climate reform programme advocates. Rejecting the motion is consistent with C's market-oriented climate strategy and the defence of fiscal stability.

citations.quote: The EU's emissions trading system is among the most effective tools we have, and we want to make it even more ambitious and open it up to more countries that wish to join.
The fiscal framework shall be safeguarded and strengthened, and Sweden's long-term economic stability shall be defended.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motions (Kerstin Lundgren item 38 and Jonny Cato item 11) on EU labour market legislation that the committee wishes to reject. The party actively pursues a more flexible labour market and has pushed through a historic labour market reform in this direction. Supporting the committee's rejection of the party's own motions contradicts its documented position — voting No supports the party's reservation.

citations.quote: During the most recent term of office, the Centre Party pushed through a historic labour market reform that means greater flexibility for companies and better transition opportunities for employees.
The Swedish labour market needs both more flexibility and more security. Support for transition and further training must improve.
citations.princip: flexibility and security in the labour market

motivering: The Centre Party upholds labour immigration but wants the labour market to operate with fair conditions. A raised self-sufficiency requirement strengthens migrants' position and counters social dumping, which is consistent with C's line of an open but well-regulated labour market. C does not support V's motion to reject the requirement.

citations.quote: Protect labour immigration. In order for Swedish companies to be able to compete, they must have the opportunity to quickly find, recruit and hire the right skills.
The Swedish labour market needs both more flexibility and more security.

motivering: The Centre Party upholds the rule of law and wants governmental systems to maintain high integrity. Strengthening the coordination number system (samordningsnummer) with better identity checks is in line with C's rule-of-law principles. V's motion on easier access without proper controls runs counter to this line.

citations.quote: The rule of law and the rights of the individual vis-à-vis the state must be defended.
shall become even more transparent. We want to establish an anti-corruption authority, tighten rules against corruption and introduce a lobbying register. •

motivering: The Centre Party upholds press freedom and the rights of cultural creators, and supports EU cooperation. The EU directive on copyright in the digital single market gives press and rights holders better protection online, which aligns with C's principles of press freedom and free culture. The committee's rejection of the motion means the directive is implemented as planned.

citations.quote: Comprehensive, independent and vigorous media coverage throughout the country is essential for democracy. Press freedom must be protected and independent public service broadcasting defended.
Academic and artistic freedom, as well as free culture, are cornerstones of a vital civil society.

motivering: The committee rejects V's motion on debt enforcement following inadequate credit assessment. C has no motion in this vote and the manifesto does not cover these insolvency law matters specifically. C's market-oriented principles speak against restricting creditors' options without a clear documentary basis, and C votes with the committee.

citations.quote: Sweden needs more free trade and international cooperation, not protectionism and closed borders. Sweden needs more freedom and enterprise.

motivering: The committee proposes that the Riksdag reject a motion submitted by Malin Björk et al. (C). The party should support its own motion and vote against its rejection. Faster prosecution — including more efficient sentencing — is in line with the party's demand for shorter processing times in courts and a stronger justice chain.

citations.quote: Lead times for processing and the exercise of public authority in courts and agencies must be shortened and access to legal representation improved.
Sweden needs more police officers, tougher sentences and better preventive measures — with vigorous action against gang crime, violence against children and men's violence against women.

motivering: The committee proposes rejecting motions on more hospital beds, shorter queues, and freedom of choice in healthcare. These demands directly coincide with the Centre Party's own reform goals of shortening queues, creating more hospital beds, and protecting freedom of choice. The party should support these motion demands by voting no to the committee's rejection, regardless of the motioners' party affiliation.

citations.quote: We want to shorten the queues and create more hospital beds where needed through investments in more nurses and better state support for the regions
citations.princip: shorter queues and more hospital beds

citations.quote: We want to defend freedom of choice in healthcare and social care and conduct operations close to the care recipients.
citations.princip: freedom of choice in healthcare and social care

motivering: The vote concerns the rejection of V's (the Left Party's) motion (point 3) on Agenda 2030 in public financial management. C prioritises fiscal discipline and prudent use of taxpayer funds, not a left-wing model with government directives on sustainability goals in budget management. C supports the committee's rejection and votes Yes.

citations.quote: The fiscal framework shall be protected and strengthened, and Sweden's long-term economic stability shall be defended. Policy shall be prudent with taxpayers' money. More money shall be spent on the core of the welfare state, less on benefits.
citations.princip: fiscal discipline and the integrity of the framework

motivering: C has its own motion (Anne-Li Sjölund et al., point 4 on the distinct character of the non-profit sector) which the committee rejects. The manifesto highlights that the role of civil society and the popular movements (folkrörelser) is invaluable and that independent adult education (folkbildning) is of great importance when democratic values are being questioned. C votes No to protect the unique character of the non-profit sector.

citations.quote: Civil society's role in binding people together and improving integration is invaluable.
Independent adult education (folkbildning) is of very great importance in times when democratic values are being questioned.
The sports movement and Sweden's popular movements (folkrörelser) make valuable contributions to building trust and community.

motivering: The Centre Party values comprehensive and independent media coverage as essential for democracy and wants Sweden to become even more transparent. Increased transparency in the ownership of radio and television companies strengthens the democratic foundation of press freedom. The committee's proposal to implement the transparency rules is in line with C's democracy and transparency agenda.

citations.quote: Comprehensive, independent and viable media coverage throughout the country is essential for democracy. Freedom of the press shall be protected and independent public service broadcasting defended.
Sweden shall become even more transparent. We want to establish an anti-corruption authority, tighten rules against corruption, and introduce a lobbying register.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motions (Mikael Larsson et al. (C), points 1 and 3) on military defence and capability which the committee proposes to reject. The manifesto demands a two-percent target and rapid rearmament. Reservation 3 is C's reservation; the party should vote No to support its own military defence position.

citations.quote: Sweden shall be defended. We want to build up military defence quickly, powerfully, and for the long term. Sweden needs to invest two percent of GDP in defence as soon as practically possible and join NATO.

Sweden shall be defended. Russia's invasion in violation of international law has shown that we cannot rule out Sweden being drawn into war. Ukraine's heroic defence of its country's freedom and survival has shown that it is possible to stand up to despots. The Centre Party wants to build up defence, strengthen Sweden's civil preparedness, and complete the accession to NATO.
citations.princip: complete NATO accession and defence build-up

motivering: The Centre Party wants courts and authorities to shorten processing times, in line with the Swedish National Audit Office's criticism of the long waiting times in the migration courts. The committee's proposal to close the matter with a requirement for continued follow-up is compatible with C's position. C has no own reservation in the matter and rejects V's/MP's motions.

citations.quote: in Sweden shall be able to have their case heard. Lead times for processing and exercise of public authority in courts and authorities must be shortened, and access to legal counsel improved. •
The rule of law and the rights of the individual vis-à-vis the state must be defended.

motivering: The committee rejects SD's (Sweden Democrats') motion on the authority structure in the transport sector. C has no motion in the vote and the manifesto lacks a specific position on the organisation of transport authorities. Without a clear connection to C's principles on decentralisation or infrastructure, C votes with the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: Decentralise more. People shall be allowed to decide more for themselves, and political decisions shall be made close to those affected.

motivering: The committee rejects the Centre Party's own motions (Ulrika Liljeberg, points 22, 34, 49, and Annie Lööf, point 99) on statutes of limitations for serious crimes. C supports Reservation 37. The manifestos demand tougher sentences for sexual offences and the criminalisation of controlling behaviour — rules on statutes of limitations are a natural complement to these commitments.

citations.quote: We want to increase sentences for sexual offences, serious violation of a person's integrity, and serious violation of a woman's integrity. We also want to criminalise controlling behaviour.
citations.princip: tougher sentences, perpetrators must not go unpunished

citations.quote: Men who assault shall not go unpunished.

motivering: Adding foreign espionage to the Criminal Code is a direct national security measure responding to the serious security situation. The amendments to the Criminal Code and the signals intelligence laws adjusted by the committee are directed specifically at espionage — not at general mass surveillance — and therefore do not conflict with the party's principled opposition to preventive surveillance. The Centre Party's strong defence line supports yes.

citations.quote: Sweden shall be defended. Russia's invasion in violation of international law has shown that we cannot rule out Sweden being drawn into war. Ukraine's heroic defence of its country's freedom and survival has shown that it is possible to stand up to despots.
The Centre Party wants to build up defence, strengthen Sweden's civil preparedness, and complete the accession to NATO.

omvarld.faktor: Russia's ongoing war of aggression against Ukraine
omvarld.effekt: Acute security threat justifies legislative measures against foreign espionage in the Criminal Code

motivering: The committee proposes a reasoned opinion that the EU's crisis instrument for the internal market does not in all respects comply with the subsidiarity principle, in particular regarding the definition of strategically important goods. C's decentralisation principle supports subsidiarity review that keeps political decisions close to those they affect. C votes Yes.

citations.quote: Decentralise more. People shall be allowed to decide more for themselves, and political decisions shall be made close to those affected.
Sweden needs more free trade and international cooperation, not protectionism and closed borders. Sweden needs more freedom and enterprise.
citations.princip: free internal market without unnecessary EU over-regulation

motivering: C's manifesto wants to save lakes, waterways, and seas and restore wetlands. The committee's tillkännagivande (formal request to the government) on expanded wetland investments aligns well with C's environmental agenda. SD's motions (Martin Kinnunen) on eutrophication and Baltic Sea cooperation are rejected, and C supports the committee's position.

citations.quote: Save Sweden's lakes, waterways, and seas. Our children shall be able to swim without being exposed to toxins, littering, or algal blooms.
More must be done to restore wetlands, combat invasive species, and make it easier for landowners to contribute, as voluntarism and property rights are the foundation of better nature conservation.

motivering: The Centre Party supports a well-functioning public administration with high integrity and transparency. The duty of notification between authorities strengthens the reliability of the system and counteracts misuse of coordination numbers. V's motion to limit this duty runs counter to C's rule-of-law position.

citations.quote: The rule of law and the rights of the individual vis-à-vis the state must be defended.
shall become even more transparent. We want to establish an anti-corruption authority, tighten rules against corruption, and introduce a lobbying register. •

motivering: The manifesto is explicit: natural resource values from wind power, hydropower and mines shall remain locally — one of the party's most important rural commitments. C is an opposition party and likely had motions among the anonymized [nr] motions. The party should support Reservation 13 and vote No.

citations.quote: More of the value created from natural resources — such as wind power, hydropower and mines — shall remain locally.
The profits from local power production — such as wind and water — shall to a greater extent remain in the local community.

motivering: The motions in this vote are mainly from SD and are rejected by the committee. C's manifesto emphasizes that politics should keep an arm's length distance from culture and that decisions should be made close to citizens. Without its own motions in the area of world heritage and with SD as the counterproposing party, C supports the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Academic and artistic freedom as well as free culture are cornerstones of a vital civil society. Politics should contribute to good conditions but keep an arm's length distance.
The Centre Party is now the only centre-right party that will not cooperate with the Sweden Democrats or give them power over how Sweden is governed.

motivering: C has explicitly declared that the party will never cooperate with SD or give them power. Voting No and supporting SD's reservation on student loan write-offs would be giving SD influence, which C's documents categorically reject. C's own recruitment measures for healthcare (graduation bonus, examenspremie) also differ substantially from SD's proposal.

citations.quote: The Centre Party is now the only centre-right party that will not cooperate with the Sweden Democrats or give them power over how Sweden is governed. We stand firm on that.
We want to recruit more nurses by introducing a graduation bonus and providing pay during specialist study periods.

motivering: The committee rejects both extremes: SD's motion against composition requirements and MP's motion for mandatory requirements in corporate boards. C's manifesto supports gender equality in entrepreneurship but through incentives and redistributed venture capital, not mandatory quotas. Rejecting both extreme positions is consistent with C's market-based and libertarian approach.

citations.quote: Sweden ranks low in international comparisons of women's entrepreneurship. We want to reform the social insurance system so that more women can invest in entrepreneurship and ensure that public venture capital is distributed more equally.
It should be easy to start and run a business; it should pay off to take the step and invest.

motivering: C pushed through a historic labor market reform with better transition opportunities via the social partners — its preferred market-based channel. V's and S's proposals for expanded state study loan policy for transition reflect a more state-centered approach that deviates from C's liberal line. The committee's rejection with reference to ongoing work is compatible with C's reform.

citations.quote: During the last parliamentary term, the Centre Party pushed through a historic labor market reform that means greater flexibility for companies and better transition opportunities for employees.
Support for transition and further education must improve.

motivering: C has its own motion (Ulrika Heie et al., point 4 on equal and equitable public transport) which the committee wishes to reject. The manifesto asserts that a society without gender equality is not fair and that public transport should become smoother and more attractive. C votes No to support its motion on equitable public transport.

citations.quote: We are liberals because we believe in individual freedom and the equal worth of all. A society without gender equality is not fully free; a society without gender equality is not truly fair.
citations.princip: equal worth of all and gender equality

citations.quote: Emission-free transport, bicycles, electric cars and public transport shall become smoother and more attractive.

motivering: The committee rejects the Centre Party's own motion point 2 (Helena Lindahl et al.) on storage of biometric data. C's reservation (Alternative A, Reservation 5) protects individual privacy against the state's collection of biometric data, in line with the party's principle that individual rights vis-à-vis the state must be defended. C votes No and supports its own reservation.

citations.quote: We therefore say no to stop-and-search zones, collective punishment, reversed burden of proof, anonymous witnesses, preventive wiretapping and restrictions on freedom of religion.
The rule of law and individual rights vis-à-vis the state must be defended.

motivering: The committee proposes to reject an explicit C motion (Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist et al. (C), point 22) on Visit Sweden AB. The tourism industry's good conditions are part of rural and growth policy. Reservation 15 represents C's position; the party should vote No.

citations.quote: The tourism industry is of great importance for the development of the whole country, and for it to continue to grow, better communications and infrastructure are also required.
It is unreasonable that local producers of alcoholic beverages cannot sell their products to visitors. Allow farm sales of alcohol to strengthen the tourism industry and develop the rural areas.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motions (Annie Lööf et al. (C), point 50, Helena Lindahl et al. (C), point 18) on the regionalization of property tax which the committee proposes to reject. Decentralization and local self-determination are cornerstones of the manifesto. Reservation 11 is C's reservation; the party should vote No.

citations.quote: Decentralize more. People should be allowed to decide more for themselves, and political decisions should be made close to those affected.
The shoreline protection rules shall be reformed to make it easier to build and live in rural areas. It is time to give rural residents more self-determination over their own land.

motivering: The matter concerns approval of a new goal for foreign trade, exports and investment promotion. C's manifesto strongly emphasizes free trade and open markets as necessary for Swedish companies' competitiveness. S's alternative motions are rejected by the committee. C supports the free-trade-oriented new goal and votes Yes.

citations.quote: Sweden cannot manage without free trade. Open up more markets for Swedish goods and services. Impose stricter requirements on working conditions, the environment and the climate in trade agreements.

the whole life. Sweden also needs political leadership that sees the rest of the world as an opportunity, not as a threat — that opens up new markets for Swedish goods and services and makes it possible to recruit employees from other countries.

motivering: The committee proposes a tillkännagivande (formal request) against building high-speed rail and rejects the Centre Party's own motions (Ulrika Heie, Annie Lööf, Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist). The manifesto states that C wants to 'build new main lines from north to south' and make a major investment in rail traffic. Voting Yes would be going against the party's own motions and clear infrastructure priorities. C supports the reservation (alternative A) and votes No.

citations.quote: We want to upgrade regional railways, build new main lines from north to south, raise the standard of the national main line network across the whole country and make a major investment in tomorrow's rail traffic — for the benefit of the climate and rural areas.

motivering: None of the Centre Party's motions are among the rejected points — it is S motions that are rejected. The manifesto underlines that the importance of sports, outdoor recreation and culture for public health is undeniable, but gives no specific instruction for action in this vote. The committee's reference to ongoing work gives no reason to vote against the proposal.

citations.quote: The importance of sports, outdoor life and culture for public health is undeniable. Providing culture throughout the country is an important starting point for the Centre Party.

motivering: The committee rejects the Centre Party's own motion (Annie Lööf et al., C, motion 131) on expropriation compensation. The manifesto explicitly demands that 'compensation for appropriated land be paid at considerably higher amounts than today.' Voting Yes means the party votes against its own motion. C supports the reservation (alternative A) and votes No.

citations.quote: compensation for appropriated land be paid at considerably higher amounts than today
State authorities must cooperate and work land-efficiently when taking new land for roads, railways, electricity, etc.

motivering: C's green reform agenda establishes that the Centre Party puts the climate first and that the future must be green. Welcoming a positive account of the Agenda 2030 work is consistent with this commitment. The Finance Committee's proposal to note the communication and reject motions that lack support in C's sustainability ambitions is supported.

citations.quote: The Centre Party puts the climate first, because the future must be green.
We can meet the climate and environmental challenge and hand over a sustainable planet to future generations.

motivering: Motions from SD, S and MP on museum matters are rejected. C has no motions of its own in the committee report and has no specific commitment to new museum legislation. The principle that politics should 'keep an arm's length' from culture argues for supporting the committee's rejection rather than pursuing the counter-proposal's line.

citations.quote: Academic and artistic freedom as well as free culture are cornerstones of a vital civil society. Politics should contribute to good conditions but keep an arm's length.

motivering: The legislative amendment closes a loophole that allowed legal entities to acquire agricultural property without an acquisition permit and aims to preserve the balance between individual owners and companies. This aligns with the Centre Party's values on strong agriculture, food security and property rights for individual landowners. SD's reservation (alternative A) undermines this protection. C votes Yes with the committee.

citations.quote: Forestry needs good conditions grounded in strong property rights.
A long-term sustainable food supply with increased supply security and increased food production requires deregulation and tax cuts

motivering: C recognises segregation as a 'main priority' but combats it primarily through jobs, the work-first principle and integration — not through S's and MP's more state-driven action packages. C's liberal approach means it does not support motions with emphasis on state redistribution over work and personal responsibility.

citations.quote: Sweden is segregated between those with and without jobs, between those who were born here and in other countries, between those with and without education. Reversing this must be a main priority ahead of the next term of office.
Integration efforts should be characterised by hard work and high expectations.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motion (Martina Johansson et al., motion 1) on the pension system that the committee wishes to reject. The party has contributed to pension increases and has a clear commitment to defending the pension system's long-term fairness and sustainability. No means that the party supports its own reservation and its own pension positions.

citations.quote: Sweden's pensioners must have good security, now and for many years to come. That is why the Centre Party contributed to a major increase in pensions, especially for those with lower incomes. We must defend the pension system's long-term fairness and sustainability.

motivering: The vote concerns the rejection of V's motion (motion 3) on sickness benefit and disability. C's programme emphasises the work-first principle and that those who are able to work should not live on taxpayers' money. V's left-wing position on expanded sickness benefit runs counter to this. C supports the committee's rejection and votes Yes.

citations.quote: The work-first principle must be upheld, and those who can work should not live on taxpayers' money.
citations.princip: the work-first principle over welfare dependency

citations.quote: We want to improve rehabilitation and make sick leave more flexible.

motivering: The committee rejects the Centre Party's own motions (Alireza Akhondi et al., motions 6–8 and 34, Annie Lööf et al., motion 26) on a review of the National Land Survey (Lantmäteriet). The manifesto's emphasis on property rights, land-efficient land use and reliable public services throughout the country clearly indicates that the party wanted to see improvements. C supports the reservation (alternative A) and votes No.

citations.quote: State authorities must cooperate and work land-efficiently when taking new land for roads, railways, electricity, etc. Likewise, compensation for appropriated land must be paid at considerably higher amounts than today.
Public services should be close and reliable throughout the country.

motivering: The committee rejects the Centre Party's own motions (Ulrika Heie et al., C, motions 5, 10 and 11) on public transport. The manifesto clearly supports making emission-free transport and public transport smoother and more attractive, and highlights rural transport needs. The party votes No and supports the reservation (alternative A) that carries C's own positions.

citations.quote: Emission-free transport, bicycles, electric cars and public transport should be made smoother and more attractive.
It should also be easy to choose alternatives to the car in favour of trains, buses, boats and bicycles.

motivering: C's manifesto explicitly demands that employer contributions be reduced to make it cheaper to hire, especially for a company's first employee. The committee rejects C's own motions — motion 5 (Thand Ringqvist et al.) and motion 3 (Lindahl et al.) — on a reduction of social insurance contributions for small businesses. C should support Reservation 2 and vote No against the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: Employer contributions need to be reduced, initially for a company's first employee, for people who are far from the labour market as well as those with low incomes.
citations.princip: reduced employer contributions for small businesses

citations.quote: It must become cheaper and easier to hire, especially people who are far from the labour market.

motivering: The Cultural Affairs Committee proposes to reject the Centre Party's own motion 1 (Catarina Deremar et al.). The alternative is Reservation 3, which is C's own reservation in support of their motion. The party cannot vote to reject its own motion and should instead support Alternative A to defend its own position on gambling regulation.

citations.quote: Clear out the regulatory thicket for entrepreneurs, big and small.
citations.princip: C's own motion — support the reservation

citations.quote: It should be easy to start and run a business; it should pay off to take the leap and invest.

motivering: The government proposes raising VAT on repairs from 6 to 12 per cent. The Centre Party has an unambiguous commitment to not participate in tax increases, and the party also wants to make the economy more circular — more expensive repairs make reuse more difficult. Both of these documented positions point unequivocally towards No.

citations.quote: We will not participate in any tax increases that harm jobs, personal savings, or make it more expensive to live.

Sweden should become the world's most resource-efficient country and the economy more circular. With the right support and deregulation, we can recycle and reuse everything from clothes to minerals and metals.

motivering: The matter concerns specific sanction fees linked to pharmacy supervision — a regulatory issue not covered by the Centre Party's election manifesto. The government has already committed to investigating adequate measures, including price caps. With no motion of its own and no clear documentary basis for the counter-proposal (Reservation 4), the party supports the committee's position.

citations.quote: We want to defend freedom of choice in healthcare and social care and conduct operations close to service users.
citations.princip: freedom of choice in healthcare and social care

motivering: The committee rejects the Centre Party's own motions (Anders W Jonsson et al., C, motions 1–4) on care capacity, waiting times, and workforce supply. The manifesto explicitly demands shorter waiting times and more inpatient beds 'with the help of a capacity billion.' Voting Yes would be voting against C's own demands for improved healthcare. C supports the reservation (alternative A) and votes No.

citations.quote: We want to create more inpatient beds where they are needed with the help of a capacity billion and better support for the regions.
citations.princip: More inpatient beds and shorter waiting times

citations.quote: Sweden needs a healthcare and social care system that puts patients, service users, and staff at the centre.

motivering: The committee's tillkännagivande (formal request to the government) is based directly on the Centre Party's own motions (Stina Larsson et al., motions 11 and 32) on expanded investment in wetlands. The manifestos explicitly state that more must be done to restore wetlands and protect aquatic environments. Yes is a natural consequence of the party's own motions.

citations.quote: More must be done to restore wetlands, combat invasive species, and make it easier for landowners to contribute, as voluntary action and property rights are the foundation of better nature conservation.
Save Sweden's lakes, waterways, and seas. Our children should be able to swim without being exposed to toxins, littering, or algal blooms.

motivering: The Centre Party protects the rights of cultural creators and supports the implementation of the EU directive, which gives rights-holders stronger contractual protection and the press the right to remuneration online. V's motions 2–5 on an alternative implementation lack support in C's documents, which emphasise free culture and freedom of the press within the framework of EU cooperation.

citations.quote: Academic and artistic freedom, as well as free culture, are cornerstones of a vital civil society. Policy should contribute to good conditions but maintain arm's-length distance.
Comprehensive, independent, and robust media coverage throughout the country is essential for democracy. Freedom of the press must be protected and independent public service broadcasting defended.
citations.princip: freedom of the press and media independence

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motions (Mikael Larsson et al. (C), motions 11–13 and 18) on civil defence and capability that the committee proposes to reject. The manifesto is clear: civil defence is vital and preparedness must be built up. Reservation 5 is C's reservation; the party should vote No.

citations.quote: Civil defence is also vital. We must build up civil defence and society's preparedness for war and crisis.

Sweden must be defended. Russia's invasion in violation of international law has shown that we cannot rule out Sweden being drawn into war. Ukraine's heroic defence of its country's freedom and survival has shown that it is possible to stand up to despots. The Centre Party wants to build up defence, strengthen Sweden's civil preparedness, and complete the accession to NATO.

motivering: No Centre Party motions are identifiable among the rejected proposals, and the manifesto lacks specific positions on home insurance, damages, or debt relief. The general principle of a strengthened victim perspective is not sufficient to justify supporting the reservation (alternative A) when the content is unknown. C votes Yes with the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: The victim perspective must be strengthened. Those who have been subjected to crime must receive redress and better support.

motivering: The proposed 90 percent tax on electricity producers' excess revenues primarily affects wind power and nuclear power — sectors the Centre Party wants to expand significantly in order to double emissions-free electricity production. A steep profit tax risks dampening investment appetite in renewable energy and runs counter to the party's general opposition to new taxes.

citations.quote: We want to double the production of emissions-free electricity and upgrade and expand the electricity grid. At least 50 TWh of emissions-free electricity must begin to be built during the next parliamentary term.
We will not contribute to any tax increases that harm jobs, personal savings, or make housing more expensive.

motivering: V's motions (1, 2, and 4) on the future design of the Health and Medical Services Act likely concern increased state control and restrictions on private providers, which runs counter to the Centre Party's freedom-of-choice line and the principle that the regions should retain responsibility for healthcare. The committee's proposal to reject the motions is consistent with C's reform agenda for proximate and free healthcare.

citations.quote: We want to defend freedom of choice in healthcare and social care and conduct operations close to service users. Responsibility for healthcare must not be transferred from the regions to the state.
citations.princip: freedom of choice and regional governance of healthcare

motivering: C submitted its own budget alternative (Annie Lööf et al., motion 1) with diverging guidelines for economic policy. The party's programme requires a reduction in the overall tax burden and no tax increases that harm jobs, while the government's package includes, among other things, higher taxes on alcohol and tobacco. The committee's proposal rejects C's motion and approves the government's guidelines. C supports Alternative A (its own reservation) and votes No.

citations.quote: The overall tax burden must come down in the next parliamentary term. We will not contribute to any tax increases that harm jobs, personal savings, or make housing more expensive.
citations.princip: reduced tax burden, no tax increases

citations.quote: The fiscal framework must be safeguarded and strengthened, and Sweden's long-term economic stability must be defended. Policy must manage taxpayers' money responsibly. More money should go to the core of welfare, less to benefits.

omvarld.faktor: Inflation of 10.9% and rising interest rates are eroding households' purchasing power
omvarld.effekt: Reinforces C's demand for lower taxes and an alternative budget in opposition to inflation-driven measures

omvarld.faktor: GDP is expected to turn negative in 2023 (recession)
omvarld.effekt: Strengthens the opposition's argument for different priorities than the government's budget

motivering: The Centre Party wants to make preschool accessible to all children in order to strengthen gender equality and give every child a good start. The S motions rejected by the committee aim to improve preschool conditions, partially in line with C's agenda. C supports Reservation 1 in opposition to the government's line and votes No.

citations.quote: We want to make preschool and leisure activities accessible to all, without these costs burdening the municipalities, in order to facilitate integration, strengthen gender equality, and give every child a good start in life.
You should have access to an equivalent school throughout the country, with the goal of world-class education and knowledge outcomes.

motivering: The amendments to TF (the Freedom of the Press Act) and YGL (the Fundamental Law on Freedom of Expression) restrict the right to communicate information (meddelarfriheten) in cases connected to foreign espionage, which creates direct tension with the party's strong commitment to freedom of the press. The serious security situation, with an ongoing Russian war of aggression, nonetheless weighs heavily enough to justify this constitutional amendment, which the Riksdag already adopted at the mandatory first vote in April 2022.

citations.quote: Sweden must be defended. Russia's invasion in violation of international law has shown that we cannot rule out Sweden being drawn into war.
Freedom of the press must be protected and independent public service broadcasting defended.
citations.princip: freedom of the press must be protected

omvarld.faktor: Russia's ongoing invasion of Ukraine
omvarld.effekt: The security crisis tips the balance towards accepting restricted freedom to communicate information under TF/YGL for foreign espionage offences

motivering: The Centre Party submitted its own motions on children and young people online (Catarina Deremar, motion 15; Ulrika Liljeberg, motion 29; Annie Lööf, motion 23) which are now being rejected by the committee. Reservation 11 reflects C's own motions on a safe digital environment for children and young people. C votes No against the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: School should be a safe place — free from racism, homophobia, and gender-based harassment — where children can grow and develop. Better pupil wellbeing provision is a prerequisite for this.
citations.princip: safe environment for children and young people

citations.quote: The level of mental ill-health among our children and young people is far too high and we must work more preventively and create easy pathways to care, so that children and young people quickly receive care regardless of whether it concerns milder mental ill-health or psychiatric illness.

motivering: Centerpartiet (Malin Björk et al.) has submitted its own motion against the current secrecy provision for data identifying electrical installations in electricity support cases (Ch. 28, §4b). The committee rejects this motion, which is why C should vote No (Alternative A: Reservation 2) and mark its position. The party's transparency profile supports a restrictive stance toward new secrecy in public administration.

citations.quote: shall become even more transparent. We want to establish an anti-corruption authority, tighten rules against corruption and introduce a lobbying register. •

motivering: Helena Lindahl et al. (C) submitted motions 12 and 13 on corporate law matters including modernisation of the Bookkeeping Act — these are now rejected by the committee. C's election manifesto emphasises regulatory simplification and better conditions for business. C votes No to defend its own motions on modern and simplified corporate regulations.

citations.quote: Clear up the regulatory swamp for entrepreneurs, large and small. We want to introduce a new and simplified business form for micro-enterprises, so that more people will dare to try running a business.
Access to capital is crucial for many small businesses. We want public venture capital to become more effective and for the investment deduction to be broadened and deepened.
citations.princip: access to capital and growth conditions

motivering: Centerpartiet is explicitly pro-EU and wants to deepen international cooperation, which fundamentally supports payment of the EU contribution. However, the committee's proposal rejects the party's three own motions (Kerstin Lundgren motion 37, Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist motion 26, Helena Lindahl motion 31). Since Reservation 1 (Alternative A) represents C's alternative EU budget positions, the party votes No to support its line against the government.

citations.quote: Sweden needs more free trade and international cooperation, not protectionism and closed borders.
The EU's emissions trading system is among the most effective tools we have, and we want to make it even more ambitious and open it up to more countries that wish to join.

motivering: Centerpartiet wants to build new trunk railway lines from north to south and make a major investment in rail for the sake of the climate and rural areas — an explicit election policy commitment. The committee's tillkännagivande (formal notice) to say no to high-speed rail directly contradicts this, and C's motion 43 (Ulrika Heie et al.) is rejected. C supports Reservation 40 and votes No.

citations.quote: We want to upgrade regional railways, build new trunk lines from north to south, raise the standard of the national trunk railway network across the country and make a major investment in tomorrow's rail traffic — for the sake of the climate and rural areas.
citations.princip: new trunk lines and rail investment

citations.quote: The whole country is needed, from suburb to industrial town, from city to countryside. All parts of Sweden shall experience increased freedom, security and accessibility in the next term of office.

motivering: Centerpartiet advocates freer markets and wants to clear up the regulatory swamp. The committee's proposal to reject stricter marketing rules for gambling is consistent with C's liberal orientation toward reduced state control of market communication. Reservation 1 represents a more regulation-heavy line that the manifesto does not support.

citations.quote: By creating freer markets and improving competition, we can dampen prices further.
Clear up the regulatory swamp for entrepreneurs, large and small.

motivering: Centerpartiet wants to simplify regulations and reduce bureaucracy to unlock the growth potential of rural areas, which supports the Swedish National Audit Office's (Riksrevisionen) recommendation to prioritise digitalisation of property formation. The committee's proposal to note the report confirms that digitalisation is prioritised, in line with C's agenda for the efficiency of public services.

citations.quote: Expensive, complicated and innovation-stifling regulations lie like a wet blanket over parts of rural Sweden. We will clear out superfluous rules and bureaucracy.
Forestry needs good conditions grounded in strong property rights.

motivering: Centerpartiet has not submitted its own motion on drinking water sources in this report and is not among the parties in Reservation 30. The committee notes that work is already under way, which is consistent with C's pragmatic approach. In the absence of its own reservation, C votes with the committee.

citations.quote: Save Sweden's lakes, waterways and seas. Our children shall be able to swim without being exposed to toxins, littering or algal blooms.

motivering: The committee rejects C's own motions (Demirok 79/81 and Lööf 13) on the conditions for student grants and loans (studiemedel). The party cannot vote Yes and thereby support the rejection of its own motions. Reservation 1 is likely C's dissenting opinion, and C votes No to defend its position on improved student grant conditions and lifelong learning.

citations.quote: Everyone who wishes shall have the opportunity to study throughout their entire life.
Support for transition and further education must improve.

motivering: Centerpartiet supports the principle that it should cost more to pollute, which is consistent with the EU's solidarity contribution on fossil fuel profits. However, C's motion on the purpose of the tax was rejected by the Finance Committee — the party likely held a different view on how the revenue should be used. With Reservation 1 as Alternative A, C votes No to signal its alternative position.

citations.quote: It shall cost more to pollute.
citations.princip: fossil emissions must bear their cost

citations.quote: We want to stop all energy trade with Russia and phase out fossil fuels.
We will not contribute to any tax increases that harm jobs, personal savings or make housing more expensive.

omvarld.faktor: Electricity price SE3 SEK 3.27/kWh (December 2022)
omvarld.effekt: Extremely high energy prices justify the solidarity contribution and support for affected households, strengthening the basis for the tax

omvarld.faktor: Inflation CPI 11.5 % (November 2022)
omvarld.effekt: High inflation reinforces households' need for financial support and makes the question of the tax's purpose politically central

motivering: Unlike the Defence Committee (FöU) matters on cyber, military and civil defence — where C has its own named reservations — there is no explicit C motion in the critical infrastructure vote. Reservation 16 originates from S, SD or MP. Without its own C reservation, the manifesto's general support for the ongoing total defence (totalförsvar) work indicates that C should support the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: We need to strengthen Sweden's total defence (totalförsvar), reinforce the entire chain of justice, invest in preventive measures and an equitable school.

motivering: The motions on a marine environment act were submitted by V and MP, not by Centerpartiet. C is not included in Reservation 29. The manifestos support protection of the marine environment but do not call for a new separate marine environment act. The committee refers to ongoing work, which C can accept.

citations.quote: Save Sweden's lakes, waterways and seas. Our children shall be able to swim without being exposed to toxins, littering or algal blooms.

motivering: C has its own motions (2–6) on expenditure ceilings, expenditure frameworks and revenue for 2023–2025. The party's budget prioritises a lower tax burden and fiscal discipline with a different profile from the government's frameworks. The committee's proposal rejects all C motions and approves the government's proposal. The party supports its reservation (Alternative A) and votes No.

citations.quote: The total tax burden must come down in the next term of office. We will not contribute to any tax increases that harm jobs, personal savings or make housing more expensive.
citations.princip: own budget alternative with lower taxes

citations.quote: The fiscal framework shall be protected and strengthened, and Sweden's long-term economic stability shall be defended. Policy shall make prudent use of taxpayers' money. More money shall be spent on the core of the welfare state, less on benefits.

omvarld.faktor: Inflation 10.9 % and interest rate 2.5 % squeeze households
omvarld.effekt: Justifies C's demand for alternative expenditure frameworks with a lower tax burden

omvarld.faktor: Expected recession and negative GDP growth in 2023
omvarld.effekt: Reinforces C's opposition to the government's framework structure in favour of its own alternative

motivering: The committee rejects the Centre Party's own motion (Malin Björk et al., point 15) on repatriation of remains and museum objects. C supports its reservation 24 and votes No. The party's principled support for minority protection and free, independent culture underpins this position.

citations.quote: strengthen, among other things, the right to property, the prohibition of discrimination, minority protection and the position of minority languages, and constitutionally protect the right to abortion and reproductive health
Culture shall be free and independent

motivering: C's documents provide no specific support for social contribution exemptions for non-profit associations, and C has not submitted its own motions in the matter. The committee rejects motions from SD, V and MP. C does not cooperate with SD and does not share V's and MP's view on labour market policy, which is why the committee's proposal is supported.

citations.quote: The Centre Party is now the only centre-right party that will not cooperate with the Sweden Democrats or give them power over how Sweden is governed. We stand firm on this.
The role of civil society in binding people together and improving integration is invaluable.

motivering: The Centre Party holds that culture shall be free and independent and that politics should maintain an arm's-length distance. The motions from V and MP may entail more government control of children's and youth culture, which is contrary to C's view of culture. C has no motions of its own identified in this sub-matter and supports the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Academic and artistic freedom, as well as free culture, are cornerstones of a vital civil society. Politics should contribute to good conditions but maintain an arm's-length distance.
Culture shall be free and independent, sport equal and inclusive.

motivering: Muharrem Demirok et al. (C) point 16 and Jonny Cato et al. (C) point 12 on conditions for developing preschool are rejected by the committee. C's manifesto emphasises that preschool shall be accessible to all children to strengthen gender equality and integration. C supports Reservation 8 and votes No.

citations.quote: We want to make preschool and leisure activities accessible to all, without these costs falling on municipalities, in order to facilitate integration, strengthen gender equality and give every child a good start in life.
It is time to unleash the growth potential of rural areas.

motivering: The rejected motions are almost exclusively from SD concerning conditions and restrictions for religious communities. The Centre Party explicitly says no to restrictions on freedom of religion and safeguards the independent role of civil society. C has no motions of its own in the matter and supports the committee's rejection of SD's restrictive position.

citations.quote: We therefore say no to stop-and-search zones, collective punishment, reversed burden of proof, anonymous witnesses, preventive surveillance and restrictions on freedom of religion.
citations.princip: religious freedom and rule of law

citations.quote: The role of civil society in binding people together and improving integration is invaluable.
citations.princip: the independent role of civil society

motivering: Alireza Akhondi et al. (C) point 7 on the payment plan in debt restructuring (skuldsanering) is rejected by the committee. C safeguards the principle that legal and financial opportunities shall not be reserved for those with high incomes. Reservation 9 supports C's point on improved debt restructuring and C votes No.

citations.quote: The ability to bring proceedings against the state or a municipality, when one has good grounds to have one's case reviewed, shall in a liberal democracy not be a right reserved for those with high incomes. We want to create a possibility for individuals to receive compensation for legal counsel in administrative matters when they have had grounds to have their case reviewed.

Everyone living in Sweden shall be able to have their case reviewed. Processing times for administration and the exercise of authority in courts and agencies must be shortened and access to legal counsel improved.
citations.princip: right to legal review for all

motivering: The vote concerns the rejection of V's motion (point 1) on housing policy. C prefers market-oriented reforms — abolished amortisation requirements, reformed shore protection (strandskydd), regulatory simplification — rather than V's model of state intervention. C supports the committee's rejection and votes Yes.

citations.quote: The reinforced amortisation requirement — a forced saving for those with the lowest incomes — should be abolished as the interest rate environment now normalises.
Shore protection (strandskydd) shall be reformed so that it becomes easier to build and live in rural areas.

motivering: C's manifesto emphasises that culture shall be 'free and independent' and that political decisions shall be made close to citizens. A national cultural schools act as proposed by MP risks centralising cultural policy in conflict with C's decentralisation principle. The committee's rejection is consistent with C's position.

citations.quote: Decentralise more. People shall have greater self-determination, and political decisions shall be made close to those affected.
Culture shall be free and independent, sport equal and inclusive.

motivering: C's own motion (Helena Lindahl et al., point 8) on support for civil society is rejected by the committee, which rules out Yes. The counter-proposal (Reservation 1) comes from SD, and C's manifesto explicitly rules out cooperation with SD. Abstain marks C's own position on a strengthened civil society.

citations.quote: The Centre Party is now the only centre-right party that will not cooperate with the Sweden Democrats or give them power over how Sweden is governed.
The role of civil society in binding people together and improving integration is invaluable.

motivering: C's own motions (Ulrika Heie points 48–49 and Annie Lööf point 98) on charging facilities are rejected by the committee. The manifesto explicitly requires that it shall be simple to install charging for electric vehicles and that charging points shall be available throughout the country. No supports C's reservation and the green transition agenda.

citations.quote: It shall be simple and inexpensive to install solar panels, install charging for electric vehicles and reduce energy use at home — whether one lives in a house or an apartment.
There shall be ample charging points along our roads and in our car parks throughout the country.

motivering: The matter concerns the Social Democrats' motion on the global initiative 'Global Deal' for decent work — an initiative not mentioned in the Centre Party's election manifesto. The party's path to better global working conditions runs through requirements in trade agreements, not specific global partnerships. Without its own motion and without documentary support for Reservation 15, the party supports the committee's position.

citations.quote: Impose stricter requirements on working conditions, the environment and climate in trade agreements.
Sweden needs more free trade and international cooperation, not protectionism and closed borders.

motivering: The Centre Party wants to strengthen environmental governance and holds that 'it should cost more to pollute'. A motion to develop the tax on chemicals in electronics is in line with the party's goal of a more resource-efficient and circular society. The committee's rejection of this motion means that a step towards clearer environmental governance is dismissed, which speaks against the party's green reform agenda.

citations.quote: It shall cost more to pollute.

Sweden shall become the world's most resource-efficient country and the economy more circular. With the right support and regulatory simplifications we can recycle and reuse everything from clothing to minerals and metals.

motivering: The committee rejects the Centre Party's own motion (Stina Larsson et al., motion item 35) on a system for emissions trading in the Baltic Sea. The party manifesto explicitly states that C wants to make emissions trading even more ambitious and open it up to more countries. C supports reservation 13 and votes No.

citations.quote: The EU's emissions trading system (ETS) is among the most effective tools we have, and we want to make it even more ambitious and open it up to more countries that wish to join.

motivering: C supports flexible sick leave and support for people with disabilities, but the channels for this are health insurance and the LSS (Act concerning Support and Service for Persons with Certain Functional Impairments) — not an expanded state student finance policy. The proposals from V and S on student loans during sick leave and for people with disabilities reflect a more expansive state model that departs from C's liberal line. C supports the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: We want to improve rehabilitation and make sick leave more flexible.
If you have a disability, you should receive the support you need, and the state must take greater responsibility for ensuring that the LSS functions properly.
citations.princip: support via LSS, not student finance

motivering: The motions are from S and concern children's and young people's influence and participation. C's manifesto lacks specific commitments on a statutory right to influence for children and young people. C's decentralisation principle suggests that such matters should be decided locally, which supports the committee's rejection of S's motions.

citations.quote: Decentralise more. People should be able to decide more for themselves, and political decisions should be made close to those affected.

motivering: No C motion item is named in the matter. Reservation 9 originates exclusively from SD and V — parties C does not cooperate with. The manifesto takes no position on SJ AB's corporate governance. Without a motion of its own or a reservation, C should support the committee's proposal to note the report.

citations.quote: We want to upgrade regional railways, build new main lines from north to south, raise the standard of the national main railway network across the whole country, and make a major investment in the rail services of tomorrow — for the sake of the climate and the rural areas.
citations.princip: railway investment across the whole country

motivering: The Centre Party wants those granted a residence permit to be given the opportunity to support themselves, which supports a minimum wage level for work permits. The proposal aims to strengthen the position of workers and counteract wage dumping — not to close the door on recruitment from abroad. The reservation from V/MP does not offer a more credible liberal line, and C supports the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: Those who receive a residence permit should be quickly integrated and given the opportunity to support themselves.
Protect labour immigration. For Swedish companies to be able to compete, they must have the ability to quickly find, recruit, and hire the right skills.

motivering: The question of preventing pharmacies from charging excessive prices for state-subsidised medicines is not specifically covered by the Centre Party's 2022 election manifesto. The government has already committed to investigating this. Without a motion of its own and without clear documentary support for Reservation 3, the party supports the committee's proposal to close the matter.

citations.quote: Sweden needs healthcare and social care that places patients, users, and staff at the centre. This is a top priority for the Centre Party ahead of the next electoral term.
citations.princip: healthcare and social care centred on the patient

motivering: The PLO model (price and wage adjustment mechanism) ensures productivity requirements and predictability in state appropriations, which is in line with C's commitment to 'making good use of taxpayers' money' and protecting the fiscal policy framework. C has not submitted its own motions in the matter, and V's motion item to change the PLO arrangement is not in keeping with C's principle of order and discipline in public finances. The committee's proposal to note the report is supported by C.

citations.quote: The fiscal policy framework must be protected and strengthened, and Sweden's long-term economic stability must be defended. Policy must make good use of taxpayers' money. More money should be spent on the core of the welfare state, less on benefits.
citations.princip: fiscal policy framework and public finance order

citations.quote: Responsible leadership that strengthens Sweden's economy in the long term and defends order and discipline in the economy and the fiscal policy framework.

motivering: C's own motion item 11 in the motion by Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist et al. was rejected by the committee in the report on state ownership. C advocates free enterprise and limited state ownership, and the committee's dismissal of C's position means that C should support the counter-proposal (Reservation 2) rather than the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: Sweden needs more free trade and international cooperation, not protectionism and closed borders. Sweden needs more freedom and enterprise.
It should be easy to start and run a business; it should pay off to take the leap and invest.

motivering: The Centre Party emphasises that the role of civil society in bringing people together is invaluable. A positive account of the distribution of funds from Allmänna arvsfonden (the General Inheritance Fund) to civil society projects is welcomed in line with this support. The committee's proposal to note the report and reject the counter-demand is supported, as the opposing motion's requests have no basis in C's documents.

citations.quote: The role of civil society in bringing people together and improving integration is invaluable.
citations.princip: support for the role of civil society

citations.quote: The sports movement and Sweden's popular movements (folkrörelser) make valuable contributions to building trust and community.
citations.princip: the social value of popular movements

motivering: The Swedish National Audit Office's (Riksrevisionen's) report on digital doctor consultations and locum doctors is being handled by the National Board of Health and Welfare (Socialstyrelsen), which the government refers to. The Centre Party lacks documentary support for pursuing stronger parliamentary demands in this narrow area and has no reason to vote with SD's reservation. Noting the report is consistent with the party's line that healthcare's administrative processes should be improved through the right tools.

citations.quote: The administrative burden in healthcare must be reduced, including with the help of digital tools that are practical and in demand among staff.
We want to defend freedom of choice in healthcare and social care and conduct activities close to care recipients. Responsibility for healthcare must not be transferred from the regions to the state.

motivering: The Centre Party maintains that environmental taxes must be powerful and preserve their real steering effect. GDP indexation ensures that the taxes are not eroded by economic growth and CPI movements, which supports the principle that it should cost more to pollute. Rejecting indexation would mean weakened environmental governance, which runs counter to C's green reform agenda.

citations.quote: It should cost more to pollute.
citations.princip: Preserve the steering effect of environmental taxes

citations.quote: Sweden shall become the world's most resource-efficient country and the economy more circular.

motivering: C has an explicit commitment to build up defence 'quickly, powerfully, and in the long term' and to invest two per cent of GDP 'as soon as it is practically possible'. The committee rejects C's own motion items 8 and 9 on military and civil defence by referring to work already under way, which does not satisfy C's demand for rapid rearmament. C should support Reservation 1 and vote No.

citations.quote: We want to build up the military defence quickly, powerfully, and in the long term. Sweden needs to invest two per cent of GDP in defence as soon as it is practically possible and join NATO.
Civil defence is also vitally important. We must build up civil defence and society's preparedness for war and crisis.

motivering: V's motion 3 on increased resources in healthcare is likely aimed at centralised state financing rather than C's model with regional responsibility and freedom of choice.
